column1: # internal/tui file -> target package assignment (Session 1.5, Phase 0).
# One row per production .go file under internal/tui, one target package each.
# Paths are relative to internal/tui. Columns: path, package, layer, basis.
# `basis` is how the row was decided: `assigned` means the file was read and
# placed by what it declares; `receiver:T` means Go pins it, because a method on
# T cannot cross a package boundary, so the file must land wherever T lands.
# Layers are the graph in context.md: L0 presentation/theme/textfit/taskref/
# status/pulse/keymap, L1 chrome/coordinator, L2 grammar/query, L3 operation,
# L4 route, L5 listsurface, L6 help, L7 notes|taskdetail|taskform|lens|conflict
# then projecthub then outliner, L8 tui (root shell).
# One assignment corrects context.md rather than follow it, and Session 1.6
# should treat it as a finding, not a typo:
#   - outliner_mode.go and outliner_mode_style.go are chrome, not outliner: the
#     mode catalog is vocabulary that operation, route, lens, projecthub and
#     query all read, so it cannot sit at L7.
# Twelve rows were corrected while their package was being extracted:
#   - view_accent.go is route, not theme (Session 2.1). It resolves a
#     PresentationID to an accent category and only then asks theme for a color,
#     so its whole vocabulary is route's; assigned to theme it was the one file
#     that made an L0 package call upward into L4.
#   - app_errors.go is status, not tui (Session 2.6). It declares errorCmd
#     alone, whose entire body constructs the ErrorMsg that app_messages_core.go
#     already sends to status; leaving it in the shell would have split a
#     message from its only constructor across a package boundary for no gain.
#     Session 2.6's completion contract names the file explicitly.
#   - operational_title.go is pulse, not chrome (Session 2.7). Session 1.5 read
#     it as a header renderer over theme styles and the mode catalog and put it
#     at L1; Session 2.7's completion contract names it as pulse's, and the
#     export budget settles it. The title row is the only reader of the pulse
#     ladder and of TodayPaceReadout, so splitting the two forces
#     and TodayPaceReadout public for one consumer, while keeping them together
#     leaves every one of them unexported. Its one genuine chrome dependency,
#     the mode chip, stayed behind as operationalTitleModeSegment in
#     outliner_mode_style.go, which is where the mode catalog already lives.
#   - cursor.go is chrome, not listsurface (Session 2.8). It declares ClampCursor
#     and HalfPage, two integer functions over a cursor and a window, and its
#     nine production consumers span L2 to L7: grammar's autocomplete.go is one
#     of them, and grammar may import only chrome, theme, textfit and taskref, so
#     at L5 the file was unreachable from its own caller. At L1 every consumer
#   - fullscreen_task_helpers.go is chrome, not taskdetail (Session 2.8). It
#     imports image/color, lipgloss, models, pulse and theme and nothing else,
#     declares the shared full-screen title row and renderPriorityBadge, and is
#     read by text_editor.go, parent_selector.go, tag_add_shared.go and
#     column_layout.go. Session 2.8's brief names it through its
# Eight more rows were corrected by Session 2.8 in the other direction: they
# were assigned chrome but reference identifiers above L1, so they stayed in
# package tui with a corrected row, the shape Session 2.4 established for
#   - contextual_action_sheet.go is listsurface, not chrome. It is built on
#     ListSurfaceModel and thirteen more listsurface types, and reads
#   - operation_text_prompt.go is route, not chrome. It names twelve operation
#     (*AppModel).newOperationTextPrompt, which pins that half to the shell.
#   - parent_selector.go, tag_selector.go and tag_add_shared.go are listsurface,
#     not chrome. All three are ListSurfaceAdapter pickers, and the two tag ones
#   - picker_items.go is query, not chrome. Every declaration left in it is a
#     method on TagInfo, which tag_filter_selector.go declares in query, so Go
#   - view_helpers.go is outliner, not chrome. TitleParams and
#     buildTitleFilterSuffix read query's SortField, SortByDefault and
#   - app_messages_footer_flash.go is tui, not chrome. footerFlashTick reads
#     footerFlashFrameInterval, whose sibling footerFlashFrames lives in the
#     AppModel-pinned footer_flash.go; this is app_errors.go's rule from Session
#     2.6 pointing the other way, keeping a message, its constructor and its two
# Test files are deliberately absent. They follow the production file they
# audit, except the uitest harness and the registry-union parity tests, which
# context.md keeps in the root shell.
